title: Potential US Population Impact of the 2017 ACC/AHA High Blood Pressure Guideline
authors: Muntner P, Carey RM, Gidding S, Jones DW, Taler SJ, Wright JT Jr, et al.
population: Participants of the US National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2011 to 2014 with three standardised blood-pressure measurements, weighted to the US adult population; all seven authors are listed among the writing committee of the 2017 ACC/AHA guideline (PMID 30354655)
funder: Paul Muntner receives research support through grant 15SFRN2390002 from the American Heart Association.
authorConflicts: Muntner has received research support and honoraria from Amgen, Inc., stated as unrelated; all other authors report no disclosures.
result: The crude prevalence of hypertension among US adults was 45.6% (95% CI 43.6% to 47.6%) by the 2017 ACC/AHA definition (130/80 mm Hg) against 31.9% (30.1% to 33.7%) by JNC7 (140/90 mm Hg); antihypertensive medication was recommended for 36.2% against 34.3%. Among adults taking antihypertensive medication, 53.4% were above the 2017 goal against 39.0% above the JNC7 goal. 103.3 million US adults had hypertension by the 2017 guideline, of whom 81.9 million were recommended medication.
